title: RE: RE: ForgeSight - admin/user management for the pilot
raw_text:
From: Marcus (Head of Product)
To: Priya (Eng Lead), Tom (Sales)
Cc: Dana (Customer Success)
Subject: RE: RE: ForgeSight — admin/user management for the pilot
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 17:41

Agreed on all of it. Priya, take the three below as decided and I'll put them in the pilot scope.

One addition of my own before you do: an admin must be able to export the list of users and their assigned roles as a CSV. Meridian's IT team reviews access quarterly and they will not do it by screenshotting a web page.

M.

> From: Priya (Eng Lead)
> To: Marcus (Head of Product), Tom (Sales)
> Subject: RE: ForgeSight — admin/user management for the pilot
> Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:02
>
> Two of the three are fine and one needs a decision from you.
>
> Fine: an admin can invite users in bulk by uploading a CSV of email addresses. Northwind is 340 seats and nobody is typing those in one at a time.
>
> Fine: Every enterprise buyer wants to know that an inactive session logs itself out after thirty minutes. We'll do exactly thirty, configurable later, not in the pilot.
>
> Needs a decision: when an admin deactivates a user, what happens to the dashboards that user built? My strong preference is that deactivating a user must not delete the dashboards they built; ownership transfers to the account admin. Otherwise somebody leaves the company and a team loses its Monday report.
>
> Separately, and I want this written down because it will otherwise be assumed away: the pilot supports Chrome and Edge only. We are not testing Safari or Firefox before November.
>
> P.
>
> > From: Tom (Sales)
> > To: Priya (Eng Lead), Marcus (Head of Product)
> > Subject: ForgeSight — admin/user management for the pilot
> > Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:20
> >
> > Three things came out of the Meridian and Northwind calls this week, all
> > about administration rather than charts, and all three are the sort of
> > thing that stalls a deal in procurement rather than losing it outright.
> >
> > First, seat loading. Northwind will not hand-enter 340 users and said so.
> >
> > Second, security. Every enterprise buyer wants to know that an inactive session logs itself out after thirty minutes. Meridian's reviewer asked for the exact number.
> >
> > Third, leavers. Both accounts asked what happens to a person's dashboards
> > when that person leaves. I did not have an answer and it showed.
> >
> > Tom
